definitions.explanation: Casual form of {端|はし} meaning 'edge' or 'end.' The っこ ending adds a familiar, slightly affectionate tone, often used in everyday conversation and with or by children.

examples.english: I love the end pieces of the bread.
I left the key on the edge of the desk.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ソファ→ソファ：04485_sofa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{端|はし}っこ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}って→座る：00757_suwaru⟧⟦{絵本|えほん}→絵本：10429_ehon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んでいた→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: The children were sitting at the edge of the sofa reading a picture book.

notes:
Casual variant of ⟦{端|はし}→端：00936_hashi⟧ formed with the diminutive/familiar suffix っこ. It carries a friendlier, more concrete feel — useful in speech but generally not in formal writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{机|つくえ}→机：00762_tsukue⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{端|はし}っこ: the edge of the desk
- ⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{端|はし}っこ: the end (heel) of a loaf of bread
- {端|はし}っこ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}る→座る：00757_suwaru⟧: to sit at the edge
- {端|はし}っこ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧: to cut off the end

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{端|はし}→端：00936_hashi⟧: edge; end (neutral, all-purpose)
- ⟦{隅|すみ}→隅：01625_sumi⟧: corner (interior corner of a room or space)
- ⟦{先|さき}→先：02883_saki⟧: tip; point (the very end, often pointed)
